nfl_predictor.cli.rankings.help: Model kind, matching the saved checkpoint (margin_total or blend; blended_margin_total also means blend).
Compute records through this week (inclusive); future games are week > this.
ML dataset (must include future game feature rows).

How teams are rated. 'composite' (default) ranks on the ETL's schedule-adjusted strength composite for the week after --through-week: the current-season view. 'bradley_terry' fits ratings to game results with the --ratings-* options. --legacy-franchise-fit implies bradley_terry.
Per-team weekly strength file written by the ETL, read by the composite method (default: data/strength_snapshots.csv).
Bradley-Terry only. Optional minimum season to include in the ratings fit. Default: include all historical seasons available in --data-schedule.
Include postseason games in records and in the Bradley-Terry fit (default: regular season only). The composite never includes postseason games.
Bradley-Terry only. How many seasons the ratings fit sees, counting the current one. Default 2 (current plus previous). Use 0 for every available season.
Bradley-Terry only. Weight applied to games from seasons before the current one. Default 0.25. Current-season games always weigh 1.0.
Bradley-Terry only. Target for completed games. 'margin' maps the observed point margin through the model's win-probability curve; 'binary' scores every win the same.

Bradley-Terry only. Feed future games' model win probabilities into the strength fit. Off by default: the fit should describe results, not the model's own forecasts. Future games always remain in projected standings.

Reproduce the historical 'franchise' ranking exactly: a Bradley-Terry fit with every season since 1999 weighted equally, binary win/loss targets, and future model probabilities in the fit. Implies --method bradley_terry and overrides the other --ratings-* flags.
